heroHeadline: Village de Dieu Offensive Day 6+; IOM: 1.5M Displaced, 18,000 from Cité Soleil in May; US Embassy Endorses Electoral Decree
heroSubtitle: The Haitian National Police Village de Dieu offensive continued through at least June 6, 2026 — the sixth consecutive day of operations against the 'Baz 5 Segonn' (5 Seconds) gang using armored vehicles, explosive drones, and tear gas along Route Nationale 2, the only road linking Port-au-Prince to Haiti's southern peninsula (severed since 2021). The PNH June 5 public safety warning — that gangs are using civilians as human shields — remains in effect; residents continue evacuating toward Martissant. The IOM confirmed June 5–6 that Haiti's displacement crisis has reached a record 1.5 million internally displaced persons, with Port-au-Prince metro IDPs exceeding 300,000 for the first time and 18,000+ newly displaced from Cité Soleil gang violence in May alone. IOM Chief of Mission Gregoire Goodstein warned: 'Haiti's displacement crisis is entering an even more alarming phase.' On June 6, the US Embassy welcomed Haiti's electoral decree as 'an important step in the process leading to elections' — reaffirming Washington's backing for the August 30, 2026 electoral framework despite PM Fils-Aimé's May 12 acknowledgment that security conditions are 'not met' for August elections. The Gang Suppression Force advance force remains at ~800 of the 5,500-person authorized ceiling, concentrated exclusively in Port-au-Prince city center. MSF's Cité Soleil emergency department and sexual violence unit remained operational as of June 6 following their June 1 reopening after 25 days of forced closure. On June 5, PM Fils-Aimé unveiled a commemorative postage stamp for Haiti's historic FIFA World Cup qualification (first in 50+ years) and announced the elimination of import taxes on batteries and solar panels at a World Environment Day ceremony. The US Supreme Court TPS ruling covering approximately 350,000 Haitian nationals (Trump v. Miot) remains pending, expected in late June–early July 2026.
